findings.title: Route inventory gate misses double-quoted handlers
findings.what: Both exact-route and startsWith collectors require single-quoted literals. A valid handler such as `pathname === "/api/new-sensitive-route"` or `pathname.startsWith("/api/private/")` produces no collected route, so the inventory validation can pass without an access classification. The tests cover only single-quoted examples.
findings.fix: Parse the server source with an AST and collect string literals independent of quote style, or minimally update both patterns to capture matching single or double quotes; add double-quoted exact and prefix regression cases.
findings.acceptance: A unit test passes double-quoted exact and prefix handlers to `collectEnterpriseRouteKeys`, asserts both are collected, and asserts an unlisted double-quoted handler makes inventory validation fail.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 287 and 297 hard-code `'([^']+)'`, while the collector test at lines 28-45 contains only single-quoted handler syntax. JavaScript accepts the omitted double-quoted forms, and neither remaining collector branch matches them.

findings.title: Multiline network constructors bypass the inbound boundary gate
findings.what: Non-fetch primitives are matched independently on each physical line. Valid code such as `new\nEventSource('/api/live')` does not place `new` and `EventSource` on the same line and therefore produces no violation, allowing a direct dashboard-server connection outside the sanctioned owner list. The regression fixture uses only a same-line EventSource expression.
findings.fix: Detect these primitives from the TypeScript AST, as already done for fetch, including NewExpression targets and navigator.sendBeacon property calls; add multiline regression fixtures.
findings.acceptance: Tests assert that multiline `new EventSource`, `new WebSocket`, and `new XMLHttpRequest` expressions outside owners are reported, while comment and string occurrences remain ignored.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed PRIMITIVE requires `new\s+<constructor>` in one regex input, but lines 175-189 apply it one line at a time. The only non-fetch primitive fixture at line 40 is same-line, so the valid multiline syntax survives both implementation and test coverage.
